native_result.query: What kind of demographic disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated?
native_result.HypoA: Gender disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated, with males having higher median wealth than females.
native_result.HypoB:
CONFIRMATION — Final candidate stands as submitted.

Deliverable recap (unchanged, ready for submission):
- QUESTION: demographic disparities in median 1985 wealth among ever-incarcerated individuals.
- ANSWER (natural-language hypothesis, descriptive): among individuals jailed 1985–1994, median composite_wealth_1985 was much lower than among the never-incarcerated (overall $720, n=289, vs $3,600, n=11,724; ~5-fold gap), with a demographic gradient within the incarcerated group: White median ≈ $2,200 (n=69) vs Black ≈ $320 (n=159) vs Hispanic ≈ $0 (n=61); the group is overwhelmingly male (252/289, male median $1,000); every race/sex incumbent stratum has lower median wealth than its never-incarcerated counterpart; low Black/Hispanic medians partly reflect very high zero-wealth shares (43–48%); female cells (n=9–16) too small to interpret; temporal caveat (1985 wealth predates 1985–1994 jail spells) noted, so the claim is descriptive, not causal.
- PAYLOAD: hypothesis populated; workflow describes the executed pipeline; executed_analysis=true.
- ARTIFACTS (local): analysis/nls_incarceration_analysis.py (executed, exit 0), analysis/median_wealth_by_group.csv, analysis/results_summary.txt.
- EVIDENCE INCLUDED IN PRIOR HANDOFF: exact medians, n per cell, bootstrap 95% CIs, sensitivity medians (exclude negatives/zeros, trimmed), and non-parametric test p-values (KW p=0.070; MW Black-vs-White p=0.047, Hispanic-vs-White p=0.041).

No further changes are required; the final candidate stands as approved.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data; normalized hispanic typo; computed median composite_wealth_1985 by race/sex/race-x-sex within ever_jailed==1 (primary) and 0 (context); sensitivity variants (exclude negatives, exclude zeros, top-1% trimmed); bootstrap 95% CIs for jailed race medians; descriptive non-parametric tests (KW + pairwise MW + jailed-vs-never per race). Final hypothesis descriptive, with temporal caveat.

sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth 1979 cohort; 1985 wealth compared by jail status during 1985–1994. The association is descriptive, not causal, because 1985 wealth predates the jail spells.
sub_hypo.relations: Median 1985 wealth was approximately one-fifth as high among ever-jailed individuals as among their never-incarcerated comparison group.

sub_hypo.text: Among individuals jailed during 1985–1994, median 1985 composite wealth was highest for White respondents (approximately $2,200, n=69), followed by Black respondents (approximately $320, n=159) and Hispanic respondents (approximately $0, n=61). sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth 1979 cohort respondents with ever_jailed=1 during 1985–1994; descriptive comparison of 1985 wealth, not a causal claim.
sub_hypo.relations: Within the jailed group, median wealth followed White > Black > Hispanic; high zero-wealth shares partly accounted for low Black and Hispanic medians.

sub_hypo.relations: Males constituted 252/289 of the jailed group and had median wealth of $1,000; no interpretable female-cell wealth comparison was asserted.

sub_hypo.text: Every race-by-sex stratum among individuals jailed during 1985–1994 had lower median 1985 composite wealth than its never-incarcerated counterpart.
sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth 1979 cohort; comparisons within corresponding race-by-sex strata. Female cells of 9–16 individuals were too small to interpret. The relationship is descriptive, not causal, given the timing of wealth relative to jail spells.
sub_hypo.relations: Within every race-by-sex stratum, median 1985 wealth was lower for ever-jailed respondents than for the never-incarcerated comparison group.
